quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, motorcycle riders should watch out for:

options.text: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked vehicles. A car may suddenly pull out from the curb or parking space.

questions.question: When you brake, you should use:

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. Using both brakes together gives you the most stopping power.

questions.question: The best gear to wear while riding is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that protects you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. This includes a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: When riding on a bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave. This is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and cross at a steady speed. Do not try to zigzag to stop the weaving, as this forces you to swerve in your lane.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is fastened securely is the single best way to increase your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, clothing:

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not cover your arms or legs completely.
Should not include a jacket if the weather is warm.
Can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: The right clothing protects you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely, even in warm weather. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but loose enough to move freely.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
The faster alcohol leaves your body.
The more likely you will avoid being stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Drinking quickly causes alcohol to build up in your body. Never ride a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Only for use if the rear brake fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe when used correctly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used properly. It provides more than three-fourths of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid hitting an object or uneven surface, you should:

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, approach it straight on at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as you can and make sure your motorcycle is upright. Rise slightly off the seat so your knees absorb some of the shock. Just before impact, roll the throttle slightly to lift the front wheel.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip.
questions.explanation: The throttle is usually on the right handle grip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: Before you ride, check that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes rub against the steering.
Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can stop the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Make sure it feels firm and stops the motorcycle when you apply it fully.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect like:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have a manual transmission. When you downshift to a lower gear, the motorcycle slows down.

questions.question: Turn signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Don't matter much because motorcycles are small.
Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Should not be used if no other vehicles are nearby.
Are harder to use than signals on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are more at risk. Use turn signals to warn other drivers about your plans. Always signal when you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one else is around.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for riding a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or shoes with high ankles give the best protection. Laced-up boots are best. High-top boots or heavy shoes work too. If your shoes have long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) are made to:

options.text: Stop the wheels from skidding and locking.
Stop brakes from working on dry roads.
Tell you when brake pads are worn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from skidding and locking.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). ABS prevents wheel skidding and lock-up during hard braking in a straight line. It works when you press both the front and rear brake controls hard. Sensors detect if a wheel might lock up. When this happens, the system releases and reapplies brake pressure to keep the best braking power.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move to the side of your lane to let them share it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If you can do it safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make it worse by encouraging them to keep tailgating at a higher speed.

questions.question: When checking tires before a ride, look at all of these except:
questions.correctAnswerText: How shiny they are
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread depth, and wear.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol and wait one hour per drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Your body can clear about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your body even at this rate. Your ability to ride and your judgment can still be impaired.

questions.question: The best riding gloves are made of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong material for good protection.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen often, so don't worry about them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can kill you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be deadly.

questions.question: Riding gloves are usually made of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are made of leather. They help you grip the handlebars and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should wear boots or shoes with soles that:

options.text: Are hard, strong, and not slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are hard, strong, and not slippery.
questions.explanation: Choose boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Pick footwear with soles made of hard, strong material that will not slip.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your clothing should:

options.text: Cover both your arms and legs.
Cover your arms but not your legs.
Cover your legs but not your arms.
Be whatever is most comfortable, even if unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover both your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: For protection while riding, wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.

questions.question: If your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks, you will:

options.text: Get more power to the rear wheel.
Lose power to the rear wheel.
Lose power to the front wheel.
Get more power to the front wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lose power to the rear wheel.
questions.explanation: If your chain or belt fails, power to the rear wheel stops immediately.

questions.question: When you are about to turn, you should:

options.text: Only use a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only use a turn signal at stop lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when turning or changing lanes. Use it even if you think no one is watching. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: Alcohol impairs your ability to ride:
questions.correctAnswerText: After the first drink.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can harm your riding ability. You can be impaired well below the legal limit. No amount of alcohol is safe before riding.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, be ready for:

options.text: A car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
Other drivers to see you and stay away.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull out in front of you. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you the most space between you and the parked cars.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:
questions.correctAnswerText: Greatly reduces head injury severity.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet greatly improves your chance of avoiding serious head and neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not block your side vision.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Stay there so you don't surprise the driver.
Wave to get the driver's attention.
Slow down until you exit the blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down until you exit the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, either speed up quickly or slow down and move back to exit the spot.
